AI-DLC Studio user guide

English | 简体中文

This guide takes you from a machine with nothing installed to a finished AI-DLC intent, and then describes every page of Studio. It covers AI-DLC Studio v2 (aidlc-studio-v2, 2.0.0 beta), which bundles AI-DLC 2.11.0 and needs KiroCrew 0.8.0 or newer.

Important

Install Bun before you do anything else. AI-DLC's engine and the hooks inside every AI-DLC conversation are TypeScript programs that Bun runs. Without Bun, Studio can still open, but it cannot install AI-DLC into a repository, create an intent, compute a plan or run AI-DLC's doctor, and AI-DLC refuses every approval and answer you send, because its hooks cannot record that a person sent them. Install it first, on the machine that runs the KiroCrew Gateway: Step 0.

Before you start

What you need
Bun Required. Install it first: Step 0
KiroCrew 0.8.0 or newer, running
Platform macOS or Linux. On Windows, run it in WSL 2: Windows
kiro-cli Signed in, as the same operating-system user that runs the gateway
Kiro plan A paid plan for the models AI-DLC expects
Git To clone Studio. In a repository it is optional: without it Studio shows "Git observation is off"
Node.js and npm Only if you rebuild Studio's UI. Installing never needs them

Where to run commands

Run every command in this guide on the machine that runs the KiroCrew Gateway, as the operating-system user that runs it. If your gateway is on a remote server or in a Docker container, run them there (docker exec -it <container> bash for a container). Repository paths you give Studio are paths on that machine too.

Words this guide uses

Term Meaning
Repository A project directory you register with Studio. Studio never finds or registers one on its own
Harness The AI-DLC files installed into a repository (under .kiro/, plus the aidlc/ workspace)
Space An AI-DLC workspace inside a repository. Each space has its own intents and team memory
Intent One piece of work AI-DLC carries through its phases, such as "add guest checkout"
Stage, Gate A step of the AI-DLC method; a Gate is a stage that stops for your approval
Checkpoint Any point where AI-DLC waits for a person: a Gate, a question, a plan approval, a missing input
Conversation The KiroCrew chat, running the aidlc agent, that one intent is bound to. Studio sends your decisions there as your own messages
Card One item in the Action Center queue

Windows: run it in WSL 2

KiroCrew itself installs directly on Windows (its official KiroCrew-Setup.exe), but Studio does not run on native Windows yet:

  • Studio's backend uses a file lock (fcntl) that exists only on macOS and Linux. In KiroCrew for Windows, Studio installs, but its backend fails to load.
  • KiroCrew on Windows does not support project skills (<project>/.kiro/skills) yet, and AI-DLC is installed in a project's .kiro/.
  • app.json declares only macOS and Linux, and Studio has not been validated on Windows.

So on Windows, run the KiroCrew Gateway in Linux under WSL 2 and use it from a Windows browser. If KiroCrew is already installed directly on Windows, quit it first: both use port 5476 by default.

Warning

This path has not been validated end to end on a Windows host yet. It relies on the Linux environment Studio already supports. If something goes wrong, attach a Diagnostic export from the Activity page to your report.

You need Windows 10 version 2004 (build 19041) or newer, or Windows 11.

  1. Open PowerShell as an administrator, install WSL 2 with Ubuntu, restart when asked and create a Linux user:

    wsl --install -d Ubuntu

  2. Open the Ubuntu terminal from the Start menu and install the basic tools:

    sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y curl unzip git

  3. Install Bun inside WSL: follow the Linux steps of Step 0 in the Ubuntu terminal. A Windows Bun installed from PowerShell is invisible to the gateway and conversations in WSL.

  4. In the Ubuntu terminal, install KiroCrew with its official one-line installer, and sign in to kiro-cli as the same Linux user:

    curl -fsSL https://download.crew.kiro.dev/cli.sh | sh

    Channels, first-run setup and upgrades are in KiroCrew's install guide.

  5. Continue with Step 1 inside WSL: clone into the Linux file system (for example ~/work).

  6. Open http://localhost:5476 in a Windows browser. WSL 2 forwards localhost ports to Windows by default. Then do Step 2 as usual.

You can also run KiroCrew's official image under Docker Desktop. This command is from KiroCrew's README and binds the port to this machine only:

docker run -d --name kirocrew \
  -p 127.0.0.1:5476:5476 \
  -v kirocrew-home:/home/kirocrew \
  ghcr.io/kirodotdev/kirocrew:stable

Then open a shell in it with docker exec -it kirocrew bash and install Bun and Studio there with the Linux steps (see the Docker installation verification).

Keep in mind:

  • Every path you give Studio is a Linux path inside WSL (or the container), such as /home/<you>/work/tasklist, including in Install from Path and Add repository.
  • Keep the projects you register in the WSL file system too, not on a Windows drive under /mnt/c/...: Windows drives are much slower through WSL, and Studio tells repositories apart by stable file identity (device and inode).

Step 0: Install Bun first

Install Bun before installing Studio, and preferably before launching KiroCrew, so that the gateway and every conversation it starts can see it. On Windows, install it inside WSL: Windows.

Why first

Studio runs AI-DLC's own engine for setup work, and AI-DLC's hooks run inside each conversation. Both need Bun. Without it:

  • the repository preflight warns bun: not found;
  • Install AI-DLC, New intent, plan previews, Run AI-DLC doctor and space changes fail with "bun was not found on PATH or in the usual install locations";
  • inside a conversation, AI-DLC's hooks fail silently, record no human turn, and AI-DLC refuses every approval and answer Studio sends for you.

macOS (13 or newer) or Linux: official installer

curl -fsSL https://bun.com/install | bash

# Make the default installation available in this terminal immediately.
export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH"
bun --version
command -v bun

bun --version prints a version number and command -v bun prints the executable's path. Keep that path; you may need it in Step 2.

On Linux the installer needs unzip. On Debian or Ubuntu, install missing prerequisites with sudo apt install curl unzip; on other distributions use their package manager.

If a new terminal reports bun: command not found, add this line to ~/.zshrc for zsh, or to ~/.bashrc for Bash (~/.bash_profile for a login shell), then open a new terminal:

export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH"

This is the official installer's default location. Use your own directory if you changed it.

Alternative: Homebrew

brew install oven-sh/bun/bun
bun --version
command -v bun

On macOS, Homebrew puts Bun in /opt/homebrew/bin (Apple Silicon) or /usr/local/bin (Intel). KiroCrew already includes those directories in every conversation's PATH.

If KiroCrew was already running

Nothing needs restarting. After Studio is installed, open Settings → About → Bun executable and click Detect Bun again, then follow Step 2.

Step 1: Install Studio into KiroCrew

Clone the v2 branch on the gateway's machine and note its absolute path:

git clone -b v2 https://github.com/warren830/kirocrew-app-aidlc.git
cd kirocrew-app-aidlc
pwd

-b v2 matters: the repository's default branch, main, is the 1.x line. The repository includes the built UI, so installing needs neither Node.js nor npm.

Option A: Install from Path in Discover (recommended)

  1. In KiroCrew, open Discover and click Add source at the bottom of the Sources list.

  2. In the External Registries panel, paste the path printed by pwd into Install from Path and click Install.

  3. Open Library, find AI-DLC Studio v2 and click Enable. If it is not listed, check whether Show enabled only is on. Once enabled, its ⋯ menu also offers Sync (for updates), Disable and Uninstall.

  4. If KiroCrew opens the app's details and asks for trust, grant it to this app only. Blanket third-party trust is not needed.

  5. AI-DLC Studio v2 now appears in the sidebar. You can also open it from Library → Open.

The path must be a directory on the gateway's machine.

Option B: The GitHub registry (installs 1.x, not v2)

This repository is also an app registry, but its app-registry.json lists the release branch, which is the 1.x AI-DLC Studio (aidlc-studio). To install 1.x this way, add https://github.com/warren830/kirocrew-app-aidlc with branch release in Discover → Add source → Add Registry, then Discover → AI-DLC Studio → Install. The gateway clones the registry itself, without your shell's proxy variables, so it needs direct access to GitHub.

Running v1 and v2 side by side

v2 installs next to 1.x under its own name and keeps its own database. The two do not share install receipts, so upgrade or uninstall a repository from the Studio that installed it, and answer each intent's decisions in one Studio only: each Studio opens its own conversation for an intent.

Step 2: Check the installation

Open AI-DLC Studio v2 → Settings and scroll to About.

  1. Bun executable should show Bun's path and version, such as /Users/you/.bun/bin/bun · 1.4.4. If it shows no path, only a Checked: list of the locations Studio searched, Bun was not found:

    • click Detect Bun again;
    • if it is still not found, run command -v bun on the gateway's machine, paste the full path into Absolute path to Bun, and click Save and verify path. Use the expanded path, not a literal ~ or $HOME. Use automatic detection returns to searching.

    A gateway started from the desktop app has a different PATH from your terminal, which is why a Bun that works in your terminal can still be missing here. Studio searches the gateway's PATH, then ~/.bun/bin/bun, /opt/homebrew/bin/bun, /usr/local/bin/bun and /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/bun. Changes apply immediately, without restarting Studio.

  2. The same row must also say AI-DLC conversations can run Bun. If it says AI-DLC conversations cannot run Bun, click Make Bun available to conversations, then Create the link. Studio creates one symbolic link, ~/.local/bin/bun, which every conversation's PATH already includes, and changes nothing else. Delete the link to undo it. This is the usual case after the official installer on a desktop-launched gateway: skipping it makes AI-DLC refuse every decision.

  3. Status should be Healthy, Bundled payload should report its files verified, and Tools should list both bun and git with versions.

From a terminal you can check the same health without changing anything:

bash scripts/kcapi.sh GET /api/apps/aidlc-studio-v2/health

A tour of the interface

  • Top bar: Action Center (with a count of what needs you), Repos, Intents, Workflow Map, Activity, Settings, and New intent on the right.
  • Scope bar, under the top bar: choose All repos or one repository, and on pages that read one intent, the intent. Every page follows this scope.
  • Execution status, at the right of the scope bar: turns running, repository leases held, recovery decisions and alerts. Polling for updates means the live event stream is not connected, so Studio re-reads on a timer: nothing is missed, updates are just slower.
  • Banners across the top report a degraded environment (with Open Settings) or an expired dashboard session (reload the page; nothing was sent).
  • Notifications: the count on the KiroCrew rail, plus optional Slack messages. See Notifications.

The interface is in English or Simplified Chinese, follows the dashboard's language by default, and has light and dark themes. AI-DLC's own words (stage names, questions, artifacts, findings and audit fields) are never translated.

Your first intent, end to end

1. Register a repository

  1. Repos → Add repository.
  2. Click Browse directories and pick the project, then Use this directory, or type its Absolute path (a leading ~ is expanded). Label (optional) is how it appears in the queue and scope bar; empty means the directory name.
  3. Click Run preflight. The read-only preflight shows the resolved path and identity, Git state, Bun's version and path, existing harnesses, the AI-DLC version and state layout on disk, free space, write permission, and any warning. Studio runs nothing in the directory and writes nothing to it.
  4. When it says This path can be registered., click Register this path.

Studio refuses a second registration of the same repository under another path (Already registered), because its leases are keyed on the repository's identity.

2. Install AI-DLC into it

Open the repository (Details) and click Install AI-DLC. The Install preview lists every managed path, who will own it, and what happens to it. Nothing has been written yet.

  • Files the framework owns are created and recorded with their digests in an install receipt.
  • Your .kiro/settings/*.json files are merge targets: Studio adds and owns only its own fragment and leaves the rest, including secrets, untouched.
  • An existing aidlc/ workspace is left exactly as it is.
  • Studio writes no AGENTS.md and no .gitignore; AI-DLC adds its own marked part to each when the first intent is created.
  • Conflicts that stop this lists any file at a managed path that differs from what Studio would install, with its diff. There is no force option: move the file aside yourself, or leave the repository as it is.

Click Install AI-DLC 2.11.0 to confirm. The transaction drawer shows each step: acquire the admin lease, stage and verify the payload, back up, write, merge fragments, validate, commit the receipt. A failure restores the starting state. If the repository changed while you read the preview, nothing is written and the preview is re-read for you to check again.

3. Create an intent

Click New intent. The wizard has four steps, and nothing is written until you click Create.

  1. Work
    • Repository: only registered repositories with AI-DLC installed can be chosen.
    • Space: AI-DLC creates an intent in its active space only. Change the active space on the repository's page (Spaces).
    • Objective: one sentence, which the engine reads as the intent's input. Start it with a word: a leading - would be read as an option.
    • Context the engine should know: optional; sent after the objective. The counter shows how many characters AI-DLC accepts for the two together. Attach a long document to the intent once it exists.
    • Label: at most three lowercase words joined by hyphens, such as guest-checkout. It becomes the intent's directory name and cannot be renamed later. Left empty, AI-DLC derives one from the objective.
    • Project type: optional; it helps the engine decide whether conditional stages apply.
  2. Preset
    • Scope: which of AI-DLC's stages are eligible. The list is read from the repository, including any scope the project defines.
    • Depth: Minimal (one pass per stage, fewer questions), Standard (questions where the engine needs you), or Comprehensive (more questions, longer artifacts).
    • Review cap: the strongest review any stage may use. none (no reviewer; Gates still need you), advisory (comments that do not block), or adversarial (findings must be answered before a Gate can pass).
    • Test strategy: Minimal (smoke), Standard (unit plus integration), or Comprehensive (adds performance validation).
    • Let the Advisor propose these settings reads your objective and the repository and proposes all of the above. Use this proposal fills the fields; you can change any of them.
  3. Plan: every stage AI-DLC knows, in its five phases, with what it produces and consumes. Turn stages on or off. A stage you cannot change says why (always runs, required by another stage, already done). If the combination breaks a dependency, Why AI-DLC will not accept this plan says what is missing. The plan diff shows what you changed against the preset and its downstream effects.
  4. Review: exact stage, Gate and artifact counts from the installed graph, estimates with their source and confidence, the products the plan declares, and the plan fingerprint. If the installed graph or scope changed since this preview, AI-DLC refuses rather than create a plan you did not see.

Click Create the intent, paused. AI-DLC writes the intent record and compiles its runtime graph; no workflow turn runs. If compilation fails after creation, click Retry runtime compilation on the same intent instead of creating another one.

4. Bind a conversation and start

Open Intents (the wizard links to it). A new intent has no conversation, so its row leads with Bind a conversation. Every decision for an intent is refused until it has one.

The conversation panel shows the repository, project and agent (aidlc) and offers:

  • Create the conversation and continue (sends /aidlc): creates a KiroCrew conversation, titles it, points it at this repository, switches it to the aidlc agent, binds it to this intent, files it in the sidebar under the repository's folder, and sends /aidlc once. It says continue because creating the intent already completed AI-DLC's initialization stages; it says start for an intent with no stage done.
  • Create and bind only: the same without sending anything.
  • Bind an existing conversation: lists conversations already open on this repository with the aidlc agent. Studio refuses any other.

With a conversation bound, Run to next checkpoint confirms and sends /aidlc. AI-DLC then works until it reaches something that needs you, fails, or completes. It never continues past a checkpoint on its own.

5. Answer checkpoints in the Action Center

When AI-DLC stops for you, a card appears in the Action Center and a notification arrives.

  1. Select the card. Read its evidence on the Decision, Artifacts, Review, Activity and Conversation tabs.
  2. Choose a decision: for a Gate, Approve or Request changes (with a note); for questions, fill in the form and Send answers.
  3. The confirmation shows the button you chose and the exact text that will be sent, for example Button: Approve → sends: …. Click Yes, send this exact text.
  4. The delivery strip tracks it: Your decision → Sent → Agent processing → State changed. The card clears only when AI-DLC's audit trail and state file show it acted on your decision, not when a request returned success.

AI-DLC continues to the next checkpoint by itself after it accepts your decision. Repeat until the workflow completes.

6. Follow progress

  • Intents shows each intent's state, current stage and progress.
  • Workflow Map draws the plan as phase swimlanes with live stage state.
  • Activity is the timeline of everything that happened, with its source.

7. Finish and commit

Studio never runs a Git write. When an intent is complete, its Intents row offers Prepare commit, which asks the intent's conversation to commit the changes the workflow made, without pushing. You confirm the exact request first. Repos → Git observation then shows the result.

Action Center

The queue

Needs you lists every card from every registered repository in the current scope. Organize it with Priority (default), Repo, Type or Oldest; Settings remembers your choice. In priority order the groups are:

  1. Recovery required and delivery uncertain
  2. Blocking Gates and questions
  3. Circuit breakers, failures, and install conflicts
  4. Requests, budget stops and pauses

Within a group the oldest comes first. Filter by repo, intent, stage narrows the list. An empty queue says Nothing needs your judgment.

Card types

Card What it means What you can do
Approval gate A stage finished and waits for approval Approve, Request changes; Accept as-is only after the engine has offered it
Question A stage cannot continue until you answer Send answers; for some checkpoints Confirm the summary, Accept the assumptions or Turn them into follow-up questions
Plan approval A stage waits for you to approve its plan Approve plan, Request plan changes
Missing input AI-DLC needs something before it can start, or asked you in the conversation Send the input; Make this the active intent when the space has no active intent
Revision in progress A stage is being revised after your feedback Information only
Recovery The evidence disagrees, or the bound conversation is lost Rebind the conversation, Record as never sent, Acknowledge
Delivery uncertain Studio cannot prove your last decision arrived Reconcile from disk, Record as never sent, Send it again
Failure The engine failed on a stage Retry now, Keep paused
Repeated failures Dispatch stopped after several failures of the same kind Retry now, Keep paused
Install conflict A Studio-managed file differs from what was installed Links to the repository's page
Budget stop A budget stopped the intent before the next turn Run now, Keep paused
Run, Resume, Prepare commit A command you started that did not go through Send it again from the card

Decision detail

  • Decision: the headline, the consequence of each choice, and the controls. A Gate also lists the stage's acceptance criteria and unresolved risks.
  • Artifacts: the files the stage produced, earlier revisions and their diff. Studio reads them and never edits them; Request changes asks the AI to revise.
  • Review: the review contract, reviewer findings grouped as open blockers, advisory or answered, and AI-DLC's review receipts. Findings are quoted verbatim.
  • Activity: this intent's events.
  • Conversation: the intent conversation's own transcript. Anything you type there is your turn.

deep link copies a link that reopens this decision.

Delivery states

State Meaning
Not sent yet Recorded, not sent
Sending Being delivered to the conversation
Sent The conversation received it
Being processed AI-DLC is working on it
Applied AI-DLC recorded it and the workflow moved
Answered AI-DLC recorded it without a workflow transition
Not sent Proven never to have reached the conversation
Needs reconciliation Delivered or possibly delivered, outcome not yet proven
Failed, Cancelled Ended without effect

Every decision is sent at most once. If the conversation was busy or another operation held the repository, nothing is sent and the card says so: send again once it is free. If you were deciding while the evidence changed, Studio shows the refreshed evidence and asks you to confirm again.

When delivery is uncertain

Studio never resends on its own. It keeps watching AI-DLC's files for the outcome. You can:

  • Reconcile from disk: re-read the files and the conversation now;
  • Record as never sent: Studio checks its own proof first and refuses if it cannot show that;
  • Send it again: queue the decision as a new item, after confirming you have read the delivery evidence. Studio refuses if it can show the first attempt arrived.

The AI Advisor

The Advisor is an optional, read-only helper running in its own session. It cannot write files, run commands, move the workflow, or reply to AI-DLC as you, and what it does is recorded in Studio's Activity only, never in AI-DLC's audit trail.

  • On a Gate: Ask the Advisor (Analyze this decision, Draft change-request feedback). It returns a reading, evidence, assumptions, alternatives and confidence. Put the drafted feedback in the box fills the note for you to edit.
  • On questions: Draft all answers, Draft this or Explain. Apply the drafted selections fills the form; Approve is never preselected.
  • On failures and recovery: Diagnose with AI.

A draft takes about three minutes. To have drafts ready when you open a card, tick the repository under Settings → Advisor → Draft ahead, per repository; this spends model usage on every card, so it is off by default.

Tool approvals

When the conversation waits for you to approve a tool call, the Intents row says so, and a notification arrives. Allow, trust or reject it in the conversation itself: Open the conversation.

Intents

One row per intent in the current scope, with its repository, state, current and next stage, progress ("3 of 33 stages done or skipped"), waiting decisions and findings. Chips mark AI-DLC's active intent, Paused and Archived. Filter by State, Space or text, and tick Include archived to see archived intents. Several intents can be in flight in one repository: turns run one at a time per repository, and different repositories run in parallel.

Button What it does
Bind a conversation / Conversation Opens the conversation panel: create, bind, Move to another conversation, Unbind, Open in KiroCrew
Run to next checkpoint Sends /aidlc once after confirmation; disabled while a turn runs, while a checkpoint waits, or when complete
Resume Sends /aidlc --resume; offered only for an intent AI-DLC parked
Open decision Opens the intent's waiting card in the Action Center
Workflow Map Opens the intent's map
Change the plan Turns pending stages ahead of AI-DLC's cursor on or off, through AI-DLC's own recompose command; sends no message
Scope and depth Previews and applies a new scope, depth or test strategy. Completed stages keep their history
Pause / Pause after current turn Stops Studio sending anything for this intent; a running turn finishes. Waiting decisions refuse to send while paused
Allow dispatch again Ends the pause; sends nothing
Archive / Restore Hides the intent from default views, in Studio only. No AI-DLC file changes. An intent with waiting decisions is paused first
Prepare commit On a completed intent: asks its conversation to commit without pushing

When the last turn stopped on a KiroCrew error, the row says so. AI-DLC keeps what it already wrote, and Run to next checkpoint picks up from there once the cause is fixed.

Unbinding only forgets which conversation the intent uses; the conversation and every AI-DLC file stay. Moving is refused while a decision for the intent may still be in flight.

Workflow Map

The map draws one intent (chosen in the scope bar) as swimlanes for AI-DLC's five phases: Initialization, Ideation, Inception, Construction and Operation. Each stage card shows its state, lead agent, Gate, review class, elapsed time and files; Executing now marks the current stage.

  • Show all stages also draws the stages this plan excludes, with the reason. Stage numbers never change. Show current plan only returns to the plan.
  • Density: Overview, Detailed, or Dependencies (draws upstream and downstream links).
  • Expand unit sub-lanes splits Construction into one lane per unit of work.
  • Show as table lists the visible stages instead.

Select a stage to open the Stage inspector: why it is or is not executing, what it consumes and produces, its files (click to open), its review contract and findings, its recent audit events, and the one Eligible operation it permits, such as opening its Gate in the Action Center. On a narrow screen the phases become accordions.

Activity

A readable timeline. Every row names its source: AI-DLC, KiroCrew, Git or AI-DLC Studio, and a Studio-derived event is never shown as an AI-DLC audit event.

  • With All repos in scope, the timeline shows Studio's own records. Choose one repository and one intent in the scope bar to read that intent's AI-DLC audit events beside them.
  • Filter by Source, stage, event, action type, severity, and time range. Older and Newer page through history.
  • Evidence on a row opens the Evidence drawer: provenance, the raw audit block (Copy the raw block), the file location and the recorded values. Credentials are removed, and paths outside the registered repository are not shown.
  • Diagnostic export produces a downloadable bundle of health, versions, settings, repositories, actions, leases, transactions and recent activity, for a bug report. It removes credentials, scrubs paths, omits artifact contents, and omits the text you sent unless you allow it in Settings first.

Repos

The list shows every registered repository with its AI-DLC state, engine version, Git state, intent count and queue count. Show archived repositories includes archived ones. Open one for its details.

Availability

If a repository is not readable, its page says why and what to do:

Shown Do this
Moved Rebind to a new path: its intents, actions and history stay attached
Permission denied Restore read access, then Rescan
Unavailable Rescan when it is back, or Unregister
Identity unprovable Resolve the duplicate directory; execution and installation stay disabled until then

AI-DLC installation and maintenance

Every operation below starts with a preview, writes only after you confirm, holds an exclusive admin lease (so it waits for a running turn and never interrupts one), and restores its starting state on failure.

Button When What it does
Install AI-DLC Not installed Installs the bundled harness with a receipt
Upgrade AI-DLC Upgrade available Moves to the bundled version. A file you changed blocks the upgrade with its diff. Retired files are removed only if unchanged
Update AI-DLC files Updated files available Applies newer files of the same version
Restore AI-DLC files Modified since install Re-creates missing files and rewrites the ones Studio may replace. Your edits block it until you resolve them
Roll back engine version After an upgrade Restores the immediately preceding compatible engine from its backups
Uninstall harness Installed Removes receipt-owned files and fragments. Workflow data, project files and changed configurable files stay, and are listed
Install recovery Install recovery required Clears a rollback that did not finish, with its own preview and validation. AI-DLC cannot run in the repository until it clears
Run AI-DLC doctor Any time AI-DLC's own health check. It adds two entries to the audit trail, so it runs only when you ask

While an install is running, Cancel and roll back installation waits for the current file operation, then restores the backups. Install history lists each transaction; open one for its steps.

Studio will not install over a newer AI-DLC than it bundles, and will not write a repository whose AI-DLC state version it cannot prove safe to migrate. Either case is shown, and the repository stays readable.

Git observation

Branch, HEAD, upstream, ahead or behind, and changed files, split into receipt-owned files with local changes (these block an upgrade), code an intent wrote that is not committed yet, and everything else. Studio only reads Git: it never commits, pushes, checks out, stashes or resets.

Spaces

Shows the active space. Create space makes a new one with fresh team memory seeded from the default space; the active space does not change. Switch space changes the repository's active space; a running turn blocks it.

Clean up transaction files

Lists the backup and failed-attempt directories transactions left outside the repository, with size and protection. Select old ones, Preview selected cleanup, then Delete the reviewed directories. Directories needed by the current installation, an active transaction or a recovery are protected. Deleting an older backup removes that rollback point.

Rename, archive, unregister

Rename repository changes its label. Archive repository hides it from the active list, keeping its files, bindings and history; restore it from Show archived repositories. Unregister forgets the registration, its bindings and its actions. None of these changes a byte inside the repository.

Settings

Studio's own preferences. Nothing here changes AI-DLC files.

Section Settings
Language and display Interface language (Follow the dashboard, English, 简体中文); Density (Compact, Comfortable)
Action queue Order the queue by: Priority, Repository, Action type, Oldest first
Automation and budgets Global concurrency: how many repositories may run a turn at once (each repository always runs one at a time); Run doctor after an install or upgrade
Advisor Offer the Advisor on decisions; Draft ahead, per repository; the Advisor model, which KiroCrew assigns
Notifications Send Slack notifications and Muted repositories; Show dashboard notifications
Diagnostics Days of activity history kept; Allow prompt bodies in a diagnostic export (off by default); days the text you sent is kept (1 to 30)
About Bun executable; Studio app and bundled AI-DLC versions; minimum and current KiroCrew version; platform; status; payload, tools, storage and reconciler health

Notifications

New Gates, questions, failures, uncertain deliveries, tool approvals and completions raise a dashboard notification. Slack messages, when KiroCrew has Slack set up, go to the owner's direct messages and cover blocking events only. A Slack message links back to Studio, where you decide: KiroCrew cannot pass a Slack button press back to Studio as a verified decision.

Unattended runs

Studio has no unattended mode. Every way of delivering text to a conversation counts as a person's turn to AI-DLC, so Studio stops at every checkpoint and sends only what you confirm.

Using Studio on a phone

The Action Center queue and the decision detail work at 390px wide, so you can read evidence and decide from a phone. Registering a repository and installing, upgrading or recovering AI-DLC are desktop-only.

Update, rebuild or uninstall Studio

Update

Update when no Studio operation is running. Pull the new code into your clone first:

git pull --ff-only

Then use Library → AI-DLC Studio v2 → ⋯ → Sync. KiroCrew re-syncs from the directory and reloads the backend.

A new Studio may bundle a newer AI-DLC. Repositories then show Upgrade available on the Repos page; upgrade each one when you choose.

Rebuild the UI

Only after editing the UI source. The locked Vite dependency needs Node.js ^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0:

(cd ui && npm ci && npm run build)   # builds ui/dist/index.mjs

Then use Library → AI-DLC Studio v2 → ⋯ → Sync.

Uninstall

To remove AI-DLC from a repository too, use Repos → Uninstall harness first: the install receipts that make a safe uninstall possible are kept in Studio's own storage. Then use Library → AI-DLC Studio v2 → ⋯ → Uninstall.

Troubleshooting

Symptom What to do
bun: command not found in a terminal Follow Step 0, add Bun to PATH, open a new terminal, run bun --version
On Windows, Bun runs in PowerShell but Studio cannot find it Studio runs in WSL: install Bun again in the Ubuntu terminal, following Step 0
Terminal runs Bun, but Studio says Bun was not found Run command -v bun on the gateway's machine, paste the result into Settings → About → Absolute path to Bun, Save and verify path
AI-DLC conversations cannot run Bun, or every approval is refused Make Bun available to conversations → Create the link
"~/.local/bin is not on this gateway's conversation PATH" Add Bun's directory to KiroCrew's agent environment (agent.env PATH) and restart the gateway
Install from Path says source is not a directory Use the absolute path of the clone on the gateway's machine (pwd in the clone)
Enable in Library opens the app's details Grant trust to AI-DLC Studio v2 there; click Enable again if needed
New intent cannot choose a repository Install AI-DLC in it, or complete its install recovery, on the Repos page
A decision is refused: "This intent has no conversation bound yet" Intents → Bind a conversation
"Another operation holds this repository" Wait for the install, doctor or turn to finish, then send again. Nothing was sent
"The situation changed while you were deciding" Read the refreshed evidence and confirm again
"AI-DLC's files disagree with each other" Open the Recovery card and follow it; nothing is sent until the files agree
"AI-DLC's active intent is not the one this decision belongs to" Studio switches the intent when it can; otherwise use Make this the active intent on the card
Delivery uncertain See When delivery is uncertain. Studio never resends by itself
Last turn stopped on an error Fix the cause in KiroCrew (the conversation offers it), then Run to next checkpoint
Page open, but AI-DLC does not run in a project Check Step 2, that kiro-cli is signed in, and that AI-DLC is installed in that repository
"Your dashboard session has expired" Reload the page. Nothing was sent

When asking for help, attach a Diagnostic export from the Activity page.
